title: Harness VLA: Steering Frozen VLAs into Reliable Manipulation Primitives via Memory-Guided Agents
summary: Exposes a frozen VLA as a retryable local contact primitive, combining task memory, global failure knowledge, and analytic control for goal rebinding and long-horizon manipulation. Improves same-backbone LIBERO-Pro success from 50.0% to 82.4%, with notes on memory, clean-to-randomized transfer, and Flash evaluation conditions.

title: World-Action Models for Robot Learning and Control: A Survey
summary: Maps the scope of World-Action Models (WAMs), joint prediction and inverse dynamics, shared-backbone and dual-system architectures, and training from video priors to action grounding. Examines predictive quality, closed-loop control evaluation, and open questions across manipulation, navigation, and driving.

title: WAFT-Stereo: Warping-Alone Field Transforms for Stereo Matching
summary: Introduces WAFT-Stereo, a stereo matching framework that replaces cost volumes with high-resolution feature warping and adds a classification-before-regression disparity initialization strategy. It reaches SOTA or Pareto-frontier performance on ETH3D, KITTI, and Middlebury while running 1.8 to 6.7 times faster than strong baselines.

title: Ask in Any Modality: A Comprehensive Survey on Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
summary: A systematic survey of multimodal RAG methods and representative works across retrieval, reranking, cross-modal fusion, context augmentation, generation, training, robustness, and agentic systems, with datasets, metrics, open challenges, and future directions.

title: PathRAG: Pruning Graph-Based Retrieval Augmented Generation with Relational Paths
summary: Proposes PathRAG, identifying that the bottleneck of current graph-based RAG methods lies in the redundancy of retrieved information rather than insufficiency. Through flow-based pruning, it efficiently extracts key relational paths between retrieved nodes, and organizes prompts in a path-structured format. PathRAG consistently outperforms SOTA baselines across 6 datasets and 5 evaluation dimensions while reducing token consumption by 13.69%.

title: HyperGraphRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Hypergraph-Structured Knowledge Representation
summary: Proposes HyperGraphRAG, the first hypergraph-based RAG method that represents n-ary relational facts (n≥2) via hyperedges, overcoming the binary-relation limitation of ordinary graphs. It includes a comprehensive pipeline for knowledge hypergraph construction, retrieval, and generation, and outperforms standard RAG and existing graph-based RAG methods across medicine, agriculture, computer science, and law domains.

title: GFM-RAG: Graph Foundation Model for Retrieval Augmented Generation
summary: Introduces the first Graph Foundation Model (GFM) for RAG, an 8M-parameter query-dependent GNN that enables single-step multi-hop retrieval. After two-stage training (self-supervised KG completion pre-training + supervised document retrieval fine-tuning), it generalizes zero-shot to unseen datasets, achieving SOTA on 3 multi-hop QA and 7 domain-specific RAG benchmarks while following neural scaling laws.

title: EvoGraph-R1: Self-Evolving Multimodal Knowledge Hypergraphs for Agentic Retrieval
summary: Proposes EvoGraph-R1, a self-evolving GraphRAG framework that reframes knowledge graphs as dynamic MDP environments. Through agent-driven actions (GRAPHRetrieve, WEBSEARCH, GRAPHEDIT, ANSWER) and GRPO optimization, it achieves closed-loop co-evolution of hypergraph structure and reasoning, attaining SOTA on multimodal VQA and text QA benchmarks.

title: Externalization in LLM Agents: A Unified Review of Memory, Skills, Protocols and Harness Engineering (2026)
summary: A systematic review of four dimensions of knowledge externalization in LLM Agents: Memory systems, Skill orchestration, Communication Protocols, and Harness Engineering — building a unified framework for agent system design and evaluation.
